text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A organizes points into clear sections (\"First of all,\" \"Second,\" \"These cars are not only expensive and contradictive\") each developed with quoted evidence from the article", "quality": "Organized argument structure", "description": "The essay presents a coherent, sequenced set of reasons, each with its own paragraph and supporting evidence, building a clear case."}, {"evidence": "Essay A quotes the article directly for each claim, e.g., the radar cost quote, the human-driver quote, and the liability question", "quality": "Evidence integration", "description": "The essay anchors each argumentative point in specific quoted details from the source text rather than paraphrasing loosely."}, {"evidence": "Essay A's thesis that driverless cars are \"not very practical\" is consistently carried through every paragraph to the conclusion", "quality": "Focused thesis development", "description": "Every body point directly supports the stated position, keeping the argument unified and on-task."}, {"evidence": "Essay A's conclusion restates the three reasons (expensive, not truly driverless, courtroom problems) and ends with a clear stance: \"Cars are better if the one driving is a human.\"", "quality": "Coherent conclusion", "description": "The essay closes by summarizing its supporting points and reaffirming its position, giving the argument a sense of completion."}, {"evidence": "Essay B makes unsupported claims like \"saving a lot of money\" and \"not having to constantly worry about wrecks\" without tying them to the article's details", "quality": "Claim substantiation", "description": "Essay A supports its assertions with source evidence while Essay B asserts benefits that are not grounded in the provided text."}]}
